summary:
Jigawa State's own criminal layer is the Sharia Penal Code Law 2000, Law No. 12 of 2000, signed into law on 18 December 2000 and brought into operation on 27 December 2000 (Jigawa State Gazette Vol. 1 No. 12). It stands under Nigeria's national framework rather than replacing it, and it adds offences the national code does not reach.

The UK Home Office country policy and information note on Nigeria (June 2025) lists Jigawa in a twelve-state table of Sharia penalties: for male same-sex conduct, married men face death by stoning, while unmarried men face 100 lashes and imprisonment of up to one year; for same-sex acts between women, the penalty is up to 50 lashes with imprisonment of up to six months. The same note confirms that the Sharia penal layer remains the operative criminal frame for Muslims in Jigawa, so a trans visitor the state reckons as Muslim is exposed to these offences and penalties directly.

The Sharia implementation sourcebook places Jigawa among four states, with Gombe, Kano and Zamfara, whose sodomy offence punishes unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm). Lesbianism carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment, and Jigawa's code includes an 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' explanation of the offence. This is conduct the federal code does not reach, including women's same-sex conduct, which means exposure in Jigawa is broader than in states without a Sharia penal layer.

Human Rights Watch (2004) records Zamfara's governor as the first to extend Sharia into criminal law, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000. By 2002 twelve northern states, Jigawa among them, had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation, and those twelve are to date the only Nigerian states where Sharia courts hold jurisdiction to try criminal cases.
tangentialFactors:
Jigawa's penalty structure for male same-sex conduct matches that of Gombe, Kano and Zamfara exactly, so the exposure described here is shared across a group of northern states rather than distinctive to Jigawa alone.

Jigawa sits within the wider twelve-state group identified by the UK Home Office in June 2025 as operating Sharia penal codes, a group that is also the only set of Nigerian states where Sharia courts try criminal cases.
localsOnly:
The UK Home Office note frames the Sharia penal layer as applying to Muslims in Jigawa; how the state determines a person's religion for that purpose is not documented in the sources available here.

Jigawa's code reaches women's same-sex conduct that the federal code does not reach, so residents face an offence here that is unavailable to prosecutors under the national statute.

Sharia courts in Jigawa hold jurisdiction over criminal cases, a jurisdiction no court outside the twelve northern Sharia states possesses.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Jigawa-specific enforcement incident — arrest, raid, prosecution, sentence or act of violence — is documented in this inventory; the record here is the text of the state code and its listing in the UK Home Office's June 2025 table.

Whether the stoning penalty (rajm) has been imposed or carried out in Jigawa is not sourced, and no date for any such sentence appears.

How a trans visitor's gender would be classified under Jigawa's code, including the 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' wording, is unresolved in these sources.
